_about: Mutation-test targets for this plugin. Each target names the file to mutate and
the test command that must notice a change (the fast module that covers it).
Run with tools/mutator.py, or as part of tools/run_tests.sh.
min_kill_rate is the floor: below it the run fails, and a target that yields no
mutants at all fails too, so a mutation pass can never be green over nothing.
per_operator caps how many occurrences of each operator are mutated (determinism
and runtime); raise it for a deeper nightly run via --max-rate/--only.

equivalent.reason: _pin_message's `getattr(pin_request, "remainingAttempts", -1)` default: the mutation changes -1 to -2, and BOTH are outside the 0..2 range that triggers the warning, so no input can tell them apart. The attribute is always present on a real Qt pinRequest and the None path is also out of range either way — proven by applying the mutant and diffing the full test output (identical rc and output).

step_index's `if count <= 0:` guard: the mutation makes it `<= 1`, and for count == 1 the guard already returns 0 - which is exactly what the clamped `min(max(current+delta,0), count-1)` returns for a one-element list. No input can tell them apart; proven by applying the mutant and diffing the full test output (identical rc and output).

targets.note: the self-reexec body is one execv a unit test cannot call without replacing the test process, so the decision (the interpreter to use, and the argv tail) is extracted into pure helpers that ARE tested

equivalent.reason: os.environ['PYTHONUNBUFFERED'] = '1' -> '2': CPython treats any non-empty value as 'on', so both disable buffering identically and no observation can tell them apart.

targets.note: its own tests drive the runner, so a mutant in the capping/slicing logic can make a nested run hang; 25 mutants and a 30s ceiling keep the target practical while still covering the runner end to end
DOM-heavy; only the extractable logic is covered so far. Targeted so the gap is measured rather than hidden, per the no-gaps rule.

equivalent.reason: BLOCK_TAGS values are only tested for truthiness; 1 and 2 are both truthy
idxOf is never called with a null element, so the guard's branch is unreachable
both operands of the guard agree on every reachable path
the out-of-range iteration is guarded by the loop body
the loop always finds an anchor before cur becomes null
two mutants on this line: the enclosing try/catch swallows the out-of-range access, and b < 4000 would need a 4000-block article
d is only ever +/-1 at this call site, so the d == 0 case is unreachable
no save is attempted during restore in any of the nine harness scenarios
with no PAGE_URL nothing is saved at all, so the flag is unobservable

`if (patched) { return true; }` -> `false`: with `false` a second call would re-wrap. Both return values lead to the same place in this script's own flow - the interval clears on the first success and the DOM-ready listener then only runs when it has nothing left to do - so no observing test can tell them apart. The re-wrap is guarded anyway: the wrap is idempotent.

`!desc || typeof desc.value !== 'function'` -> `&&`: with a missing descriptor the `&&` form dereferences `desc.value`, throws, and is caught by the same try/catch - returning false exactly as the unmutated guard does. No page-visible difference.
